Since commit 07ec77a1d4e8 (""sched: Allow task CPU affinity to be
restricted on asymmetric systems"")
user_cpus_ptr are done under pi_lock for arm64 architecture. However
dup_user_cpus_ptr() accesses user_cpus_ptr without any lock
protection. Since sched_setaffinity() can be invoked from another
process
column2: the process being modified may be undergoing fork() at

column1: the same time.  When racing with the clearing of user_cpus_ptr in
__set_cpus_allowed_ptr_locked()
column2: it can lead to user-after-free and

column1: possibly double-free in arm64 kernel.
Commit 8f9ea86fdf99 (""sched: Always preserve the user requested
cpumask"") fixes this problem as user_cpus_ptr
be cleared in a task's lifetime. However
in commit 851a723e45d1 (""sched: Always clear user_cpus_ptr in
do_set_cpus_allowed()"") which allows the clearing of user_cpus_ptr in
do_set_cpus_allowed(). This time
Fix this bug by always clearing the user_cpus_ptr of the newly
cloned/forked task before the copying process starts and check the
user_cpus_ptr state of the source task under pi_lock.
Note to stable
column2: this patch won't be applicable to stable releases.

column1: Just copy the new dup_user_cpus_ptr() function over.
